name: Music trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about composers, instruments, genres, famous songs and musicians (no lyrics quoted). Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which composer wrote the famous Fifth Symphony, first performed in 1808?
items.explain: Beethoven's Third and Fifth Symphonies premiered in 1805 and 1808, and the Fifth is among his best-known works.

items.question: The melody of "Ode to Joy" is used as the official anthem of which organization?
items.explain: Beethoven's melody, without the words, was adopted in 1985 as the anthem of the European Community, which became the European Union.

source.title: What are the lyrics to 'Ode to Joy' from Beethoven's Symphony No.9? - Classic FM

items.question: What health problem gradually affected Beethoven while he was composing?
answers: He lost the use of his hands
He lost the ability to speak
items.explain: Beethoven's first symptoms of hearing loss appeared before 1800, and his deafness became total by 1819 according to Britannica.

items.question: The Moonlight Sonata is a famous piece written for which instrument?
items.explain: The Moonlight Sonata is Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14, one of his most popular works.

source.title: Ludwig van Beethoven - Simple English Wikipedia

items.question: The "Ode to Joy" is the choral finale of which Beethoven symphony?
items.explain: The fourth movement of Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 is commonly known as the Ode to Joy and adds vocal soloists and a chorus.

items.question: Which composer wrote the opera The Magic Flute?
items.explain: The Magic Flute was Mozart's last opera, with a German libretto by Emanuel Schikaneder, and premiered in 1791.

items.question: In which city was Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born in 1756?
items.explain: Mozart was born in Salzburg and later spent his last years in Vienna.

items.question: What does the German title "Eine kleine Nachtmusik" mean in English?
items.explain: The German subtitle literally means "a little night music", and the 1787 work is one of Mozart's most famous.

items.question: About how old was Mozart when he died in 1791?
items.explain: Mozart died in Vienna in December 1791, aged 35, only a few months after The Magic Flute premiered.

source.title: The Magic Flute: Synopsis, Songs & More - English National Opera

items.question: Which Italian composer wrote The Four Seasons, a set of four violin concertos?
items.explain: The Four Seasons is the best-known work of the Italian composer Antonio Vivaldi, published in 1725.

items.question: The Four Seasons is among the most popular works of which musical era?
items.explain: Vivaldi's Four Seasons concertos are described as some of the most popular and recognized pieces of Baroque music.

source.title: 'The Four Seasons': A Guide To Vivaldi's Radical Violin Concertos

items.question: Which composer wrote the music for the ballet The Nutcracker?
items.explain: Tchaikovsky composed the Nutcracker score in 1891–1892, and he also wrote Swan Lake and The Sleeping Beauty.

source.title: Who is Tchaikovsky - San Francisco Ballet

items.question: The ballet The Nutcracker is traditionally associated with which holiday?
items.explain: The Nutcracker premiered in St. Petersburg in 1892 as a Christmas ballet and is still a seasonal favorite.

source.title: The Nutcracker by Pyotr Ilych Tchaikovsky | Music & Characters

items.question: Tchaikovsky, the composer of Swan Lake, came from which country?
items.explain: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was a Russian composer, best remembered for his ballet scores.

source.title: Who is Tchaikovsky - San Francisco Ballet

items.question: Swan Lake, The Sleeping Beauty and The Nutcracker are famous examples of which art form?
items.explain: These are Tchaikovsky's three celebrated ballet scores, among the most famous ever written for dance.

source.title: Who is Tchaikovsky - San Francisco Ballet

items.question: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
items.explain: A standard piano has 88 keys, made up of 52 white and 36 black ones.

source.title: Why does a piano have 88 keys? - Classic FM

items.question: Traditionally, the white keys on a piano were covered with which material?
items.explain: Because white keys were traditionally covered in ivory, they are often called the "ivories".

items.question: A standard string quartet has two violins, a viola and which other instrument?
items.explain: The string quartet is made up of two violins, one viola and one cello.

items.question: Which instrument is the largest member of the orchestral string family?
items.explain: The double bass is the giant of the string family, at over 6 feet long.

source.title: The String Family - All Newton Music School

items.question: Which instrument is the smallest and highest-sounding in the orchestra's string family?
items.explain: The violin is the smallest member of the string family and makes the highest sounds.

source.title: The String Family - All Newton Music School

items.question: How many strings does a standard violin have?
items.explain: A violin has four strings, typically tuned to G, D, A and E.

source.title: An In-Depth Guide on The Violin Family - Amorim Fine Violins

items.question: Which instrument did Adolphe Sax invent in the 1840s?
items.explain: The Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax invented the saxophone, which was patented in Paris in 1846.

items.question: Although it is made of brass, the saxophone is classified as part of which instrument family?
items.explain: The saxophone makes sound with a reed, like the clarinet, so it is classed as a woodwind.

source.title: The Origins of the Saxophone - Yamaha

items.question: Which small instrument plays the highest notes in the orchestra?
items.explain: The piccolo is a smaller version of the flute and plays the highest sounds in the orchestra.

items.question: Which instrument has the lowest sound in the standard orchestral brass section?
items.explain: The tuba is the lowest-sounding instrument in the orchestra's brass section.

source.title: What Instruments Are In An Orchestra? - Hello Music Theory

items.question: The large orchestral drums called timpani are also known as what?
items.explain: Timpani are also called kettle drums and can be tuned to specific notes.

source.title: What Instruments Are In An Orchestra? - Hello Music Theory

items.question: Strings, woodwinds and brass make up an orchestra along with which fourth main section?
items.explain: The four main sections of a modern symphony orchestra are strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion.

items.question: What is the name of the person who leads an orchestra and keeps the musicians together?
items.explain: The conductor leads the musicians and maintains the rhythm of the musical score.

items.question: Which section of an orchestra has the most players?
items.explain: The string family is the largest instrumental family in the orchestra in terms of players.

items.question: Which of these instruments belongs to the orchestra's brass section?
items.explain: The orchestral brass section normally includes horns, trumpets, trombones and tuba.

source.title: How Orchestras Are Structured: Sections, Roles and Conductors

items.question: Which of these instruments belongs to the orchestra's woodwind section?
items.explain: The woodwind section includes instruments such as the flute, oboe and clarinet.

items.question: In which English city did the Beatles form?
items.explain: Lennon and McCartney first performed together in Liverpool in 1957, and all four Beatles were born there.

items.question: Who was the drummer in the Beatles' best-known lineup?
items.explain: The Beatles' final members were Lennon, McCartney, Harrison and drummer Ringo Starr.

items.question: Which two Beatles were the band's main songwriters?
items.explain: The band's main songwriters were John Lennon and Paul McCartney.

items.question: Which Beatle played lead guitar in the band?
items.explain: George Harrison was the Beatles' lead guitarist, while Lennon sang and played rhythm guitar and McCartney played bass.

items.question: Which singer is known as "the King of Rock and Roll"?
items.explain: Elvis Presley is widely known as "the King of Rock 'n' Roll" and was one of rock music's dominant performers from the mid-1950s.

items.question: Graceland, the home of Elvis Presley, is located in which city?
items.explain: Graceland is Elvis Presley's estate in Memphis, Tennessee, where he lived from 1957 until his death in 1977.

items.question: Which of these films starred Elvis Presley?
items.explain: Jailhouse Rock (1957) is one of Presley's most famous films, along with Blue Hawaii and Viva Las Vegas.

items.question: In the famous "Thriller" music video, Michael Jackson dances with a horde of what?
items.explain: The John Landis-directed video shows Jackson dancing with a horde of zombies.

items.question: Which dance step did Michael Jackson popularize?
items.explain: Michael Jackson popularized a dance step called the moonwalk.

items.question: Which nickname is Michael Jackson best known by?
items.explain: Michael Jackson is widely called the "King of Pop".

source.title: The Story Behind Michael Jackson's Thriller Album - The Root

items.question: Who was the chief songwriter and lead vocalist behind "Bohemian Rhapsody"?
items.explain: Freddie Mercury wrote the mock-operatic "Bohemian Rhapsody" and sang it as Queen's front man.

items.question: Which British rock band recorded "We Will Rock You" and "Another One Bites the Dust"?
items.explain: Both songs are among the best-known hits of Queen, whose chief songwriter and singer was Freddie Mercury.

items.question: Which instrument is jazz legend Louis Armstrong best known for playing?
items.explain: Louis Armstrong began on the cornet and became the leading trumpeter and one of the most influential artists in jazz history.

items.question: Which American city is widely recognized as the birthplace of jazz?
items.explain: Jazz emerged in the cultural life of New Orleans, Louisiana, and was strongly influenced by the blues.

source.title: Music of the United States - EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: In which New York City borough was hip-hop born in the 1970s?
items.explain: Hip-hop is recognized to have originated and evolved first in the Bronx in the early 1970s.

source.title: Music of the United States - EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: What term describes the rhythmic speaking style over music that is common in hip-hop?
items.explain: This syncopated speaking style over music is known as rap, though it is not always present in hip-hop.

source.title: Music of the United States - EBSCO Research Starters

items.question: Which Tennessee city is the center of the country music industry?
items.explain: As country music grew popular, much of its music industry became concentrated in Nashville.

items.question: In which part of the United States did the blues originate?
items.explain: The blues is a type of folk song from the Southern United States, and its original form is known as Delta blues.

items.question: Which style of jazz, also known as big band music, swept the United States in the 1930s?
items.explain: Swing, or big band music, was the new form of jazz that swept the country during the 1930s.

source.title: Music of the United States - EBSCO Research Starters
